title: Enterprise Onboarding - Integration, Escalation, Health Checks & QBR Playbook
author: Asha Ramesh
body:
## Summary
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standardized approach for enterprise customer onboarding, integration validation, operational escalation, and quarterly business review (QBR) / health-check cadence. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and on-call SREs who own onboarding and post-sales reliability.

Scope: enterprise customers onboarding to Redwood Hosted API, Dedicated, or Private deployments.

Goals:
- Ensure consistent, low-friction integrations and predictable time-to-first-successful-call.
- Define clear escalation paths and SLAs for customer-impacting issues.
- Provide repeatable health checks and a QBR agenda to surface risks and optimization opportunities.

---

## Audience and Roles
- Customer Success (primary owner for onboarding and QBR cadence)
- Solutions Engineering (technical integration and verification)
- Support (1st/2nd line incident response and triage)
- Eng-SRE / Serving Runtime (3rd-line escalation for infra/runtime faults)
- Account Executive (commercial handoff, contract clauses)

Ownership matrix:
1. Pre-sales handoff: Account Exec -> CSM (deliverables: signed SOW, network IP allowlist)
2. Technical kickoff: SE -> CSM (deliverables: integration plan)
3. Go-live verification: SE & Support -> CSM (deliverables: smoke test results, monitoring configured)
4. Ongoing health & QBRs: CSM -> Customer (deliverables: QBR deck, optimization plan)

---

## Onboarding Phases & Checklist
1) Pre-kickoff (CSM / AE)
   - Confirm contract & entitlements (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
   - Collect technical contacts, network requirements, security & compliance constraints.
   - Schedule a 1-hour technical kickoff with SE and customer engineering.

2) Technical Kickoff (SE) - Agenda:
   - Introductions and roles (10m)
   - Architecture & deployment mode (10m)
   - Network & auth (API keys, VPC peering, IP allowlist) (15m)
   - Integration plan and milestones (15m)

3) Integration Implementation (SE + Customer)
   - Provide quickstart SDK examples (Python/node) and sample requests.
   - Assist with API key creation and scope.
   - Validate network connectivity (curl tests, traceroute if needed).
   - Configure observability: customer configured dashboards in Redwood Console, trace hooks, and usage alerts.

4) Validation & Smoke Tests (Support + SE) - Minimum tests to pass:
   - Auth: successful token-authenticated request returned 200 for generation/embeddings.
   - Latency: median p50 response < customer's SLA target (documented per account).
   - Streaming: verify streaming chunk delivery for long responses.
   - Edge cases: test 3 representative prompts from customer's production prompt-set.

5) Go-Live and Monitoring Handover
   - Confirm metrics are surfaced: requests/min, tokens/day, error-rate, p50/p95 latency.
   - Define alert thresholds and owners.
   - Provide runbook links and support contact channels for on-call.

---

## Escalation Playbook (Operational)
Purpose: fast, deterministic escalation for customer-impacting incidents.

Severity definitions and target SLAs:
- P0 (Severe outage): customer-facing API unavailable or >50% error rate for a paying customer in production. Initial response: 15 minutes. Engineering engagement: immediate.
- P1 (Partial outage / major degradation): request/response errors affecting >10% of requests or sustained p95 latency >2x SLO. Initial response: 1 hour.
- P2 (Functional impact): single feature regressions, elevated error rates <10%. Initial response: 4 hours.
- P3 (Informational / minor): non-urgent bugs, docs or integration help. Initial response: 24 hours.

Escalation steps:
1. Triage (Support 1st-line): validate issue, capture reproducible case, collect request IDs, timestamps, environment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), and customer impact.
2. Contain & Mitigate: apply immediate mitigations (rate-limiting, fallback model variant, temporary quota increase for Dedicated if permitted) and document actions.
3. Notify CSM & SE: Provide status update and ETA for next update. For P0/P1, call the incident bridge and notify customer via pre-agreed channel.
4. Engage Engineering (Eng-SRE / Serving Runtime): escalate to on-call per internal on-call rota with full packet (logs, traces, request IDs).
5. Post-incident: produce incident review with timeline, root cause, action items, and customer-facing summary within 48 hours for P0/P1.

Contact & escalation matrix (examples):
- Support triage queue: support+enterprises@redwood.ai (monitored 24/7)
- SE escalation: se-oncall@redwood.ai
- Eng-SRE on-call: follow PagerDuty schedule (see /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks)
- CSM escalation (account specific): included in customer onboarding packet

Communication templates:
- P0 initial notification: short, factual, ETA for first update, and steps taken.
- P0/P1 postmortem: timeline, root cause, corrective actions, and customer impact statement.

---

## Integration Guide (Developer Checklist)
Minimum integration items to validate before go-live:
- API Authentication
  - Create scoped API key for integration and rotate after verification.
  - For Private deployments: confirm KMS/HSM integration and key policies.
- Network & Security
  - If Hosted: provide IP ranges for allowlist (include egress requirements).
  - If Dedicated/Private: validate VPC peering, routes, and firewall rules.
- SDKs & Samples
  - Provide customer with language SDK snippets and Postman collection.
- Observability & Monitoring
  - Configure Redwood Console dashboards and set cost/latency alerts.
  - Instrument trace hooks if customer requires request-level attribution.
- Data & Compliance
  - Confirm data residency and retention settings; verify any redaction/PII handling requirements.

Example CURL smoke test (replace API_KEY and MODEL):

curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "redwood-1", "input": "Hello from smoke test"}' | jq

---

## Known Issues & Workarounds (Selection)
NOTE: this is a curated list of common, triaged issues seen during enterprise integrations. Keep map to internal issue tracker IDs in the customer ticket.

1) Elevated p95 latency after long prompt sequences
   - Symptom: p95 spikes when customers use very large context windows and KV cache is thrashing.
   - Workaround: recommend prefix trimming and shorter chunking; enable continuous KV cache if available in Dedicated, or suggest quantized model variant for throughput.

2) Authentication errors due to clock skew (Private deployments with signed tokens)
   - Symptom: intermittent 401s for some hosts only.
   - Workaround: ensure NTP sync; accept +/-60s skew tolerance on token validation for initial rollouts.

3) Streaming responses hang in proxies
   - Symptom: chunks stop arriving when intermediate proxies buffer responses.
   - Workaround: enable chunked transfer encoding and TTL-based keepalives on proxy; provide an SDK patch to fallback to polling for problematic networks.

4) Token accounting mismatch between customer billing and console
   - Symptom: reported tokens in customer side differ from Redwood Console by small percentage.
   - Workaround: confirm model variant and tokenizer version; run parallel test calls to sample payloads to reconcile accounting; escalate to finance if discrepancy >5%.

Each issue should include a reference to the internal tracking ID (add in ticket) and whether there is a permanent engineering fix planned.

---

## Health Checks & QBR Material
Quarterly cadence: standard enterprise customers receive a QBR every 90 days unless agreed otherwise. Health-check cadence may be weekly during first 90 days, then monthly.

Health-check metrics (minimum):
- Availability: % successful requests per day (target 99.95% for Dedicated SLA customers)
- Error rate: 5xx and 4xx per 1k requests (alert if 5xx > 0.5% or sustained increase)
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 with targets per contract (example: p95 < 350ms for Hosted baseline customers)
- Cost KPIs: tokens/day, cost per 1k tokens, trend vs. forecast
- Quality signals: regression in eval prompt-set scores, customer-reported regression tickets

QBR agenda (60 minutes):
1. Executive summary (5m) - adoption, topline metrics, and business impact
2. Operational health (15m) - availability, latency, incidents since last QBR, and action items
3. Usage & cost review (10m) - token consumption, peak patterns, forecasted spend
4. Model performance & quality (15m) - eval results, prompt-set regressions, recommendations (quantization, alternate variants)
5. Roadmap & feature asks (10m) - product changes, planned infra upgrades, and prioritization
6. Action items & owners (5m)

Deliverables for the customer after QBR:
- QBR slide deck with metrics and recommended optimizations
- Runbook updates if process changes were decided
- Project plan for any agreed migrations or performance changes

---

## Support Process & Ticketing
- Ticket ingestion: Zendesk -> Support Triage -> create internal incident in PagerDuty for P0/P1 as needed.
- Required ticket fields: customer_id, environment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), reproducible_steps, sample request_id(s), timestamps, severity.
- SLA expectations (customer-facing):
  - P0: initial acknowledgement in 15 min, regular updates every 30 minutes until mitigated.
  - P1: initial acknowledgement in 1 hour, updates every 2 hours.
  - P2/P3: acknowledgement and updates per internal SLA.

Ticket escalation checklist (Support):
1. Validate and reproduce with customer-provided request IDs.
2. Collect logs/traces (attach redwood-console links).
3. Attempt mitigation (retries, roll back config, fallback model) and document.
4. If unable to mitigate within SLA, escalate to SE and Eng-SRE with full packet.

---

## Templates & Artifacts
- Kickoff checklist (copyable): attendee list, IP ranges, API keys, sample prompts, expected go-live date, success criteria.
- Customer-facing escalation email template (P0 initial, P1 update, Postmortem summary).
- QBR slide template: title, summary metrics, incidents, optimization recommendations, next steps.

---

## Post-Incident / Post-Onboarding Review
- Within 7 days of go-live, CSM and SE perform a health audit and capture any outstanding action items.
- For any P0/P1 incidents within first 30 days of go-live, require a joint review with Product/Eng to prioritize fixes.
